source.name: Drilling Permit Master and Trailer (application type 01, new drill)

states.note: The monthly files are rebuilt by hand; the Daily report holds the newest days.

source.name: Intents to drill (master workbook and the daily file)

states.name: New Mexico
states.note: Spud dates arrive about two months late, so the series ends two months back.

states.name: Federal offshore
states.agency: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement
states.note: About 45 wells a year; spud dates arrive late.

gaps.name: Federal onshore (BLM)
gaps.agency: Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Department of the Interior
gaps.why: No free per-APD or per-well file with an approval date was found.

gaps.name: Alabama
gaps.agency: State Oil and Gas Board of Alabama
gaps.why: A free, reachable ArcGIS layer with one row per well, a PermitDate (filled for 99%, newest 2026-10-28), SpudDate, well type, county, region and coordinates; monthly permit counts can be queried directly.

gaps.name: Alaska
gaps.agency: Alaska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission, Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
gaps.why: Provisional. The agency does publish bulk and query data (a daily Access Data Extract and the Data Miner, per its own flyer and search summaries), but every host I tried is blocked from this machine: commerce.alaska.gov answered 403 (HEAD,…

gaps.name: Arizona
gaps.agency: Arizona Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (AZOGCC), administered by the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ)
gaps.why: A free, reachable ArcGIS layer with one row per permitted or drilled well (permit number, API, operator, county, TRS, lat/long, depth, formation, spud date, status and status date), updated in 2026.

gaps.name: Arkansas
gaps.agency: Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission
gaps.why: No bulk file with an issue date was found. The GIS wells layer is reachable and rich but has only a status date (text), no permit or spud date.

gaps.name: California
gaps.agency: California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM), Department of Conservation
gaps.why: The Notices map service (layer 1) is free, needs no login, answered HTTP 200 today, has one row per approved notice or permit with a determination (approval) date, a work-type column (NoticeType) and a well-type column, and is current to the day.

gaps.name: Colorado
gaps.why: Not read yet: no producer for this agency has been built.

gaps.name: Florida
gaps.agency: Florida Department of Environmental Protection, Division of Water Resource Management, Oil and Gas Program
gaps.why: A free, reachable 0.7 MB workbook with one row per permit and an ISSUE_DATE (final agency action) plus spud and completion dates.

gaps.name: Idaho
gaps.agency: Idaho Department of Lands, Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (OGCC) / Oil and Gas Program
gaps.why: Idaho has about 34 wells since 2007 (about one permit a year, none in some years).

gaps.name: Illinois
gaps.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources, Office of Oil and Gas Resource Management (data held by the Illinois State Geological Survey, ILOIL)
gaps.why: A free, reachable ArcGIS layer (no login) gives one row per well with API number, PERMIT_DATE, status, operator, elevation and lat/lon, so monthly counts of permits to drill can be built directly (192 wells dated in 2026 through Aug 28).

gaps.name: Indiana
gaps.agency: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Reclamation (Oil and Gas Program; formerly Division of Oil and Gas)
gaps.why: A free, reachable ArcGIS API gives one row per well with permit number, status, operator, lease, county, PLSS and point location, plus a completion table (CompDate, CompType, ReportType).

gaps.name: Kansas
gaps.why: Not read yet: no producer for this agency has been built.

gaps.name: Kentucky
gaps.agency: Kentucky Energy and Environment Cabinet, Department for Natural Resources, Division of Oil and Gas (Kentucky Geological Survey keeps the public well database)
gaps.why: The weekly Excel permit lists are per permit with DATE ISSUED, work type, well type, depth, formation and location: A-quality content, free, no login, current to 2026-10-23, history back to 2017.

gaps.name: Louisiana
gaps.agency: Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy (formerly Department of Energy and Natural Resources), Office of Conservation
gaps.why: Reachable, free ArcGIS layer with one row per well, PERMIT_DATE and SPUD_DATE, coordinates, depth and operator, so monthly counts of permits can be queried.

gaps.name: Michigan
gaps.agency: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE), Oil, Gas, and Minerals Division
gaps.why: ArcGIS layers 9 and 10 are free, no login, answered 200 from here, hold one record per well with PermitNumber, api_num and PermitDate (newest 2026-10-07, so maintained).

gaps.name: Mississippi
gaps.why: Not read yet: no producer for this agency has been built.

gaps.name: Missouri
gaps.agency: Missouri Department of Natural Resources, Missouri Geological Survey (staff to the State Oil and Gas Council), Rolla
gaps.why: The wells layer is shaped like an A (free ArcGIS API, API number, PERMIT_DAT issue date, SPUD_DATE, well type, status, location) but it is frozen: the newest permit is 2019-08-15 and the newest spud 2021-06-04, and confidential wells are left out, so it gives history, not current monthly counts.

gaps.name: Montana
gaps.agency: Montana Board of Oil and Gas Conservation (MBOGC), part of the Department of Natural Resources and Conservation
gaps.why: No bulk file or API with an approval date was verified. Approval dates are published only in weekly PDF letters (reachable, text-extractable, about 6 actions a week) and in the Dataminer Permits query, whose CSV export could not be driven here.

gaps.name: Nebraska
gaps.why: Not read yet: no producer for this agency has been built.

gaps.name: Nevada
gaps.agency: Nevada Division of Minerals, Commission on Mineral Resources (Oil, Gas and Geothermal / Fluid Minerals Program)
gaps.why: Free, reachable ArcGIS layer with one row per oil well (permit number, API, status including Pending and Drilling, completion date) but no approval, filing or spud date.

gaps.name: New York
gaps.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC), Division of Mineral Resources
gaps.why: One free CSV with no login, answered from here, one row per well (API number) with the application date, the permit issue date, the spud date, well type, slant, depth, formation, spacing and fee, refreshed on weekdays.

gaps.name: North Dakota
gaps.agency: North Dakota Industrial Commission, Department of Mineral Resources, Oil and Gas Division
gaps.why: The only free bulk or API source (the Wells map layer, 44,030 wells) has a spud date, well type and status but no approval date or work type, so by the grading rule it measures spuds.

gaps.name: Ohio
gaps.agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil and Gas Resources Management (DOGRM)
gaps.why: The Permit and Plug List is a well-and-permit level listing with the issue date (DT_APP_ISSUED), the receipt date, a 79-value application type, county, operator, proposed depth, formation, acres and coordinates, free and with no login, reachable from here (one POST returned 22 rows for a week).

gaps.name: Oregon
gaps.agency: Oregon Department of Geology and Mineral Industries (DOGAMI), Mineral Land Regulation and Reclamation (MLRR)
gaps.why: A free, reachable bulk spreadsheet with one row per permit (county, PLSS, lat/long, well type, depth, status, permittee) and an ApplicationDate, but no approval or issue date, no work type, and only 182 of 741 rows have a well type.

gaps.name: Pennsylvania
gaps.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Office of Oil and Gas Management
gaps.why: A for new-well permits: DEP's public ArcGIS layer is free, needs no login, answered from here, holds one row per well with PERMIT_DATE, SPUD_DATE, well type, unconventional flag and configuration, and supports server-side statistics and date filters.

gaps.name: South Dakota
gaps.agency: South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Minerals, Mining and Superfund Program (Oil and Gas), Rapid City; well database kept with the SD Geological Survey
gaps.why: A free, reachable 18 MB zip (modified 2026-10-20, no login) holds Wells.xlsx with one row per well, 'Date Permit Issued', spud, completion and plug dates, permitted and current well type (incl.

gaps.name: Tennessee
gaps.agency: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, Division of Mineral and Geologic Resources, Oil and Gas Program
gaps.why: Every TDEC data host answered 403 to one polite request from this machine (data viewer, map layer, form PDF), and no bulk file or documented API was found.

gaps.name: Utah
gaps.agency: Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining, Department of Natural Resources
gaps.why: WellHistory.csv is a free, login-free daily bulk CSV with one row per APD and work event, an APDApprovedDate, a WorkType (DRILL, REENTER, DEEPEN...) and a Slant; it joins to Wells.csv (location, operator, county, proposed depth, status).

gaps.name: Virginia
gaps.agency: Virginia Department of Energy (Virginia Energy), Division of Gas and Oil
gaps.why: The ArcGIS well layers are free, no login and answered from here, one record per well, but they hold only a status date (FiStatDt), a drilling-complete date and a well-completion date, not a labeled permit issue date, and a well leaves the 'undrilled' layer once drilled.

gaps.name: West Virginia
gaps.why: Not read yet: no producer for this agency has been built.

gaps.name: Wyoming
gaps.agency: Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (Office of the State Oil and Gas Supervisor)
gaps.why: Free, no login, reachable (200). The approved-permits export returns one row per permit/well with an Approved date (yyyymmdd), a received date, well class, horizontal flag, location and spud date, by any date range.
